questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perform the **bracket operation** first: (27 + 14) = 41.

Group all **positive terms** together: 92 + 38 + 76 + 19 = 225.

Group all **negative terms** together: 41 + 35 = 76.

Subtract the negative sum from the positive sum: 225 − 76 = 149.

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 92 + 38 − (27 + 14) + 76 − 35 + 19

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 92 + 38 − 41 + 76 − 35 + 19

⇒ 130 − 41 + 76 − 35 + 19

⇒ 89 + 76 − 35 + 19

⇒ 165 − 35 + 19

⇒ 130 + 19 = 149

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It is an acronym used to remember the **order of operations** in arithmetic. It stands for Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Commutative Property

The result of **addition** remains the same regardless of the order of the numbers: a + b = b + a.

Grouping Positive and Negative Terms

In expressions involving only addition and subtraction, calculating **positive and negative values** separately and then finding their difference is a reliable way to avoid errors.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression using the **BODMAS** rule by grouping terms.

63 + 48 − 12 + 48 − 27 + 11

Group additions: (63 + 48 + 48 + 11) = 170

Group subtractions: (−12 − 27) = −39

Final result: 170 − 39 = 131

**∴ The correct answer is 131.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 63 + 24 × 2 − (36 ÷ 3) + 48 − 27 + 11

**Rule Used:** **BODMAS** (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 63 + 24 × 2 − 12 + 48 − 27 + 11 (Solving **Parentheses**: 36 ÷ 3)

⇒ 63 + 48 − 12 + 48 − 27 + 11 (Solving **Multiplication**: 24 × 2)

⇒ 111 − 12 + 48 − 27 + 11 (Solving **Addition**: 63 + 48)

⇒ 99 + 48 − 27 + 11 (Solving **Subtraction**: 111 − 12)

⇒ 147 − 27 + 11 (Solving **Addition**: 99 + 48)

⇒ 120 + 11 (Solving **Subtraction**: 147 − 27)

⇒ 131

**∴ The correct answer is 131.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This rule dictates the **order of operations**: Brackets first, then Orders (powers/roots), followed by Division and Multiplication (left to right), and finally Addition and Subtraction (left to right).

Sign Conventions

When adding or subtracting multiple numbers, it is often faster to **group all positive numbers** together and **group all negative numbers** together before performing the final subtraction.

questions.question: A car covers a certain distance at a speed of 60 km/h. If the driver increases the speed by 25%, how much time will he save on a journey of 240 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed Ratio** (Original : New) = 100% : 125% = 4 : 5

Since **Distance** is constant, **Time Ratio** = 5 : 4

**Original Time** = 240 km ÷ 60 km/h = 4 hours = 240 min

5 units = 240 min → 1 unit (Time saved) = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 min

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original speed = 60 km/h, Distance = 240 km, Speed increase = 25%.

**Formula:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26d446b7206ee9d4fafe89be8b5afd64bd223210bf1e0c13b04e466c5afd6c27.png] 

⇒ **Original Time** = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 hours

⇒ **New Speed** = 60 + (25% of 60) = 60 + 15 = 75 km/h

⇒ **New Time** = 240 ÷ 75 = 3.2 hours

⇒ **Time Saved** = 4 − 3.2 = 0.8 hours

⇒ **Time Saved in minutes** = 0.8 × 60 = 48 min

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Inverse Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed

For a journey with different speeds for equal distances, Average Speed = 2S₁S₂ ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert hours to minutes, multiply by 60.

questions.question: Which of the following options will have sum as (11/12)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **sum** equal to 11/12, check for denominators that are factors of 12.

Convert 1/3 to an **equivalent fraction** with 12 as the denominator: 1/3 = 4/12.

Add the numerators: 4/12 + 7/12 = 11/12.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3 + 7/12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Target **sum** = 11/12.

**Formula Used:** Sum of **Fractions** = (Common Denominator method)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad0ef792e7e76fbcca886495c395fd51bcf949bbc3d1047a06a4a7c1c85bc48f.png] 

**Calculations:**

Check Option (3): 1/3 + 7/12

⇒ **LCM** of 3 and 12 is 12.

⇒ 1/3 = (1 × 4) / (3 × 4) = 4/12

⇒ 4/12 + 7/12

⇒ (4 + 7) / 12 = 11/12

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3 + 7/12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Adding Unlike Fractions

To add fractions with different denominators, first find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the denominators and convert them to **equivalent fractions**.

Equivalent Fractions

Multiplying or dividing both the **numerator** and the **denominator** of a fraction by the same non-zero number does not change its value.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A fraction where the numerator is less than the denominator is a **Proper Fraction** (e.g., 11/12), whereas one where the numerator is greater or equal is **Improper**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **decimal numbers** to simple **fractions**: 0.07/0.35 = 7/35 = 1/5 = 0.2.

Second part: 0.021/0.7 = 21/700 = 3/100 = 0.03.

Direct subtraction: 0.20 − 0.03 = 0.17.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The mathematical expression (0.07 ÷ 0.35) − (0.021 ÷ 0.7).

**Method Used:** **BODMAS rule** and **decimal simplification**.

⇒ First term = 0.07 ÷ 0.35

⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by 100: 7 ÷ 35

⇒ 7 ÷ 35 = 1/5 = 0.2

⇒ Second term = 0.021 ÷ 0.7

⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by 1000: 21 ÷ 700

⇒ 21 ÷ 700 = 3 ÷ 100 = 0.03

⇒ Final expression = 0.2 − 0.03

⇒ Result = 0.17

**∴ The correct answer is 0.17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This rule defines the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**. In this problem, division is performed before subtraction.

Decimal Point Shifting

When dividing decimals, you can shift the decimal point to the right in both the **dividend** and the **divisor** by the same number of places to work with whole numbers.

Decimal to Percentage

To convert a **decimal** like 0.17 to a **percentage**, multiply by 100 to get 17%.

questions.question: The side of a square is 21 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **square** with side **a**, the length of the **diagonal** is always **a√2**.

Given **Side** = 21 cm.

**Diagonal** = 21 × √2 = 21√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 21√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Side** of the square (a) = 21 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **square**, a diagonal divides it into two **right-angled triangles**. Using the **Pythagoras Theorem**:

Diagonal (d) = √(Side² + Side²) = √(2a²) = a√2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eda2ce293d7ce6f805a86266386a2d6279abc21eafcbcbff2e1eb403ea3812b9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(21² + 21²)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(441 + 441)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(882)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(441 × 2)

⇒ **Diagonal** = 21√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Square

The **Area** can be calculated as Side² or (Diagonal²) ÷ 2.

Perimeter of Square

The **Perimeter** (P) is the sum of all four sides: P = 4 × Side.

Ratio Property

For any square, the **ratio** of the **Side to the Diagonal** is always **1 : √2**.

questions.question: The side of a square is 22 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **diagonal** of a **square** is always **side × √2**. Given **side** = 22 cm. **Diagonal** = 22 × √2 = 22√2 cm. **∴ The correct answer is 22√2 cm.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of consecutive numbers** = Average × Total terms

**Average** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 = (11 + 30) ÷ 2 = **20.5**

**Total terms** (n) = (30 − 11) + 1 = **20**

Sum = 20.5 × 20 = **410**

**∴ The correct answer is 410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The given series is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** where the first term **a = 11**, the last term **l = 30**, and the common difference **d = 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a736abb4bbcd523728048e412d93733d366b739ce6e91b16f9e8ffb7b271d25.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Number of terms (n) = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Common difference] + 1

Sum (Sₙ) = (n ÷ 2) × (First term + Last term)

**Calculations:**

⇒ n = [(30 − 11) ÷ 1] + 1

⇒ n = 19 + 1 = **20**

⇒ S₂₀ = (20 ÷ 2) × (11 + 30)

⇒ S₂₀ = 10 × 41

⇒ S₂₀ = 410

**∴ The correct answer is 410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of first n natural numbers

The sum of numbers from 1 to n is given by the formula: [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

General term of an AP

The nth term (aₙ) is calculated as: a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.

Sum of squares of first n natural numbers

The formula to find 1² + 2² + ... + n² is: [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **total terms (n)**: n = [(Last − First) ÷ Diff] + 1 = [(96 − 16) ÷ 2] + 1 = 41.

Calculate **Average** of the series: Average = (First + Last) ÷ 2 = (16 + 96) ÷ 2 = 56.

Calculate **Sum**: Sum = Average × n = 56 × 41 = 2296.

**∴ The correct answer is 2296.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Series 16 + 18 + 20 + ...... + 96

This is an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** where:

**First term (a)** = 16

**Common difference (d)** = 18 − 16 = 2

**Last term (l)** = 96

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0af645995fb1a43d25376ea373bd1571620b559eb750a9c4acccca1281ccd2bb.png] 

**Formula Used:**

n-th term: l = a + (n − 1)d

Sum of n terms: Sₙ = (n/2) × (a + l)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 96 = 16 + (n − 1) × 2

⇒ 96 − 16 = (n − 1) × 2

⇒ 80 = (n − 1) × 2

⇒ n − 1 = 40

⇒ n = 41

⇒ Sum (S₄₁) = (41/2) × (16 + 96)

⇒ S₄₁ = (41/2) × 112

⇒ S₄₁ = 41 × 56

⇒ S₄₁ = 2296

**∴ The correct answer is 2296.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula: S = [n × (n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Sum of First n Even Numbers

The sum of the first n even numbers (2, 4, 6, ...) is given by the formula: S = n × (n + 1).

Arithmetic Progression General Term

The n-th term of an AP is aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d is the common difference.

questions.question: Average of 50 results is 'N'. 4 is subtracted from each result. What will be the new average of these 50 results?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **property of arithmetic mean**, if a constant value **k** is subtracted from every observation in a set, the **new average** also decreases by the same constant **k**.

Original Average = **N**

Value subtracted from each result = **4**

New Average = **N − 4**

**∴ The correct answer is N-4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total number of results = **50**, Old average = **N**, Subtraction constant = **4**.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9ecea326f7fbb1a43fb92fbf99b233c2f0763a8e956b57a00e9937ae54554af.png] 

⇒ Total sum of 50 results = 50 × N = 50N

⇒ Total reduction = Number of results × value subtracted from each = 50 × 4 = 200

⇒ New sum of 50 results = 50N − 200

⇒ New average = (50N − 200) ÷ 50

⇒ New average = 50(N − 4) ÷ 50

⇒ New average = N − 4

**∴ The correct answer is N-4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition of Constant

If a constant **k** is added to every observation, the new average becomes **Old Average + k**.

Multiplication by Constant

If every observation is multiplied by a constant **k**, the new average becomes **Old Average × k**.

Algebraic Sum of Deviations

The sum of the deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is **always zero**.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with counts n₁, n₂ and averages A₁, A₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question:
Average of some numbers is 'p'. 27 is the smallest number among these numbers. Which of the following statement will be always correct?

I. p = 30. II. 54 will be the largest number among these numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any set of **n numbers**, the average **p** must satisfy the condition: **Smallest ≤ p ≤ Largest**.

Given the **smallest number is 27**, we only know that **p ≥ 27** and **Largest ≥ 27**.

Since the other numbers in the set and the **total count n** are unknown, both **p** and the **largest number** can take any value ≥ 27.

Neither **p = 30** nor **Largest = 54** is a mandatory condition for all possible sets.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Smallest number in the set = 27. Average = **p**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e21d99a20698d5d979450882849bad09a0f1745d66c734a4f6accce64f1ea1c3.png] 

Let the numbers be x₁, x₂, x₃, ... , xₙ.

⇒ Smallest (x₁) = 27.

⇒ **Average (p)** = (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) ÷ n.

Checking Statement I: **p = 30**.

⇒ If set is {27, 28, 29}, **p** = (27 + 28 + 29) ÷ 3 = 28. (p ≠ 30).

⇒ If set is {27, 33}, **p** = (27 + 33) ÷ 2 = 30. (p = 30).

⇒ Statement I is **not always** correct.

Checking Statement II: **Largest = 54**.

⇒ If set is {27, 28}, Largest = 28. (Largest ≠ 54).

⇒ If set is {27, 54}, Largest = 54. (Largest = 54).

⇒ Statement II is **not always** correct.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Range of Average

The arithmetic mean or **average** always lies between the minimum and maximum values of a data set: **xₘᵢₙ ≤ p ≤ xₘₐₓ**.

Dependency on Number of Terms

To uniquely determine the **average (p)** or any specific term like the **largest number**, we must know the values of all other terms or specific properties of the distribution (like an AP).

Effect of Extremes

The **average** is highly sensitive to outliers. A very large maximum value will significantly pull the average **p** higher, regardless of the smallest value.

questions.question: What is the total number of positive factors of 180?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime factorize **180**: 180 = 2² × 3² × 5¹.

To find the **total number of factors**, add 1 to each exponent and multiply them.

Total factors = (2 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (1 + 1)

Total factors = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 factors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 180

**Formula Used:** If the prime factorization of a number N is ap × bq × cr, then the total number of positive factors = (p + 1)(q + 1)(r + 1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2174eeac4cd9c2868713608672b4866477be2f6a7b428fae34d34f1c9c2ab958.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization: 180 = 2 × 90 = 2 × 2 × 45 = 2² × 3 × 15 = 2² × 3² × 5¹

⇒ Powers are p = 2, q = 2, r = 1

⇒ Total factors = (2 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (1 + 1)

⇒ Total factors = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 factors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Factors

The sum of all positive factors of N = apbqcr is given by [(ap⁺¹−1)/(a−1)] × [(bq⁺¹−1)/(b−1)] × [(cr⁺¹−1)/(c−1)].

Product of Factors

The product of all factors of a number N is equal to N⁽Total Number of Factors / ²⁾.

Perfect Square Factors

To find perfect square factors, only consider even exponents of the prime bases in the combinations.

questions.question: What is the largest 2 digit number which is exactly divisible by both 9 and 3?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Since 9 is a multiple of 3, any number divisible by **9** is automatically divisible by **3**. We need to find the **largest 2-digit number** divisible by 9. The largest 2-digit number is **99**. Checking divisibility: 99 ÷ 9 = 11 (Exactly divisible). **∴ The correct answer is 99.**

questions.question: 50 percent of selling price of an article is equal to the 4/5 of the cost price of the article. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the parts: 50% SP = 4/5 CP ⇒ 1/2 SP = 8/10 CP

Ratio of SP : CP = 8/5

Profit = 8 − 5 = 3 units on a base of 5 units (CP)

Profit % = (3/5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

50% of **Selling Price (SP)** = 4/5 of **Cost Price (CP)**

**Formula Used:**

**Profit** = Selling Price − Cost Price

**Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b9328d67fdc9208b2ca05edb63ab2878fe7b79e8a140fc1f7966ceb38a298183.png] 

⇒ (50/100) × SP = (4/5) × CP

⇒ (1/2) × SP = (4/5) × CP

⇒ SP / CP = (4/5) ÷ (1/2)

⇒ SP / CP = (4/5) × (2/1) = 8/5

⇒ Let **Cost Price** = 5 units and **Selling Price** = 8 units

⇒ **Profit** = 8 − 5 = 3 units

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (3 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 3 × 20 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

Loss % = (Cost Price − Selling Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100. It occurs when CP is greater than SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. The discount percentage is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**.

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by CP / MP = (100 − Discount %) / (100 + Profit %).

questions.question: Cost price of 10 articles is Rs. 182. Selling price of 12 articles is Rs. 182. What is the ratio of the value of profit/loss of 1 article to the cost price of 1 article? (Cost price of all the articles is same. Selling price of all the articles is same.)
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ When the **total Cost Price** and **total Selling Price** are the same (₹182), use the inverse article ratio. Ratio of **CP : SP** = **Articles for SP : Articles for CP** = 12 : 10 = 6 : 5. Let **CP** = 6 units and **SP** = 5 units. Since CP > SP, it is a **Loss** of 6 − 5 = 1 unit. Ratio of **Loss : CP** = 1 : 6. **∴ The correct answer is 1 : 6.**

questions.question: What should be subtracted from 540 so that the number obtained will become equal to 190 percent of 110?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Target value** to be obtained = 190% of 110 = 1.9 × 110 = 209.

Required value to be **subtracted** = 540 − 209 = 331.

**∴ The correct answer is 331.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial number = **540**, Target = **190 percent** of **110**.

**Formula Used:** Subtracted Value = Initial Number − Target Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6934c534058d61f0901c28b5893081197343a971a9f8224574d7c99f330bc653.png] 

⇒ Target value = 190% × 110

⇒ Target value = (190 ÷ 100) × 110

⇒ Target value = 1.9 × 110 = 209

⇒ Let the number to be **subtracted** be x.

⇒ 540 − x = 209

⇒ x = 540 − 209 = 331

**∴ The correct answer is 331.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find x% of a value y, use the formula: (x ÷ 100) × y. Percentages greater than 100 result in a value larger than the original base.

Basic Linear Equations

In an equation of the form a − x = b, the unknown x is found by rearranging the terms: x = a − b.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

A percentage can be expressed as a decimal by dividing by 100. For example, 190% = 190 ÷ 100 = 1.9.

questions.question: Pipes P1 and P2 alone can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours respectively. Pipe P3 alone can empty the same tank in 12 hours. Firstly, both pipes P1 and P2 are opened and after 2 hour pipe P3 is also opened. In how much total time (in hours) tank will be completely filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Capacity** = LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24 units.

Efficiencies: **P1** = 4, **P2** = 3, **P3** = −2 (empty).

Work done in first 2 hr by (P1 + P2) = (4 + 3) × 2 = 14 units.

Remaining work = 24 − 14 = 10 units.

Time for remaining work with (P1 + P2 + P3) = 10 ÷ (4 + 3 − 2) = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 hr.

**Total Time** = 2 hr (initial) + 2 hr (after P3 opened) = 4 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **P1** = 6 hr, **P2** = 8 hr, and **P3** = 12 hr (emptying).

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

⇒ Work done by **P1** and **P2** in the first 2 hours = (4 + 3) × 2 = 14 units.

⇒ Remaining work to fill the tank = 24 − 14 = 10 units.

⇒ Net efficiency when all three pipes are open = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken to fill the remaining part = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 hr.

⇒ **Total Time** to fill the tank completely = 2 hr (start) + 2 hr (remaining) = 4 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

An **inlet pipe** fills the tank (positive work), whereas an **outlet pipe** (leak) empties the tank (negative work).

Net Efficiency

If multiple pipes operate together, the **net efficiency** is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies (e.g., Net = E₁ + E₂ − E₃).

Work-Time Relationship

The time taken to complete a job is **inversely proportional** to efficiency when the total work remains constant (Time = Work ÷ Efficiency).

questions.question: A car covers two distances of 35 km and 40 km in total 15 hours. Car covered both the distances at the same speed. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the car?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **speed** is constant for both distances, total speed = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ Total Time.

Total Distance = 35 + 40 = 75 km.

**Speed** = 75 ÷ 15 = 5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First **Distance** (D₁) = 35 km

Second **Distance** (D₂) = 40 km

Total **Time** (T) = 15 hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e5d8301b49fa1ce1a412eef0d83544b2f65dad8d3fda227c8d8aa1880836cd79.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D₁ + D₂

⇒ Total Distance = 35 + 40 = 75 km

⇒ **Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ **Speed** = 75 ÷ 15

⇒ **Speed** = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance-Time Formula

Speed is defined as the rate at which an object covers distance. Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a body travels equal distances at speeds x and y, the **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

questions.concept: To Make a Mixture from Two or More Things
questions.question: In a mixture alcohol and water are in the ratio of 4 : 9. Water is 25 litres more than alcohol. What is the quantity of water in the mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Alcohol** to **Water** = 4 : 9

Difference in ratio parts = 9 − 4 = 5 parts

Given: 5 parts = 25 litres → 1 part = 5 litres

Quantity of **Water** = 9 parts = 9 × 5 = 45 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 45 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of Alcohol to Water = 4 : 9 and the difference between them = 25 litres.

**Formula:** Part value = Total Value × (Required Ratio Part / Sum or Difference of parts)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31cd9138ca6892ba96a50fb4fdc545d41cc241ba6327a20eb63f7fab22c91aac.png] 

⇒ Let the quantity of **Alcohol** be 4x and **Water** be 9x.

⇒ Difference = 9x − 4x = 25 litres

⇒ 5x = 25

⇒ x = 5 litres

⇒ Quantity of **Water** = 9x = 9 × 5 = 45 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 45 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Property

If a quantity is divided into two parts in the ratio a : b, the parts are [a/(a+b)] × Total and [b/(a+b)] × Total.

Comparison of Ratio Units

When the difference between two quantities is given, identify the difference in their ratio units and equate it to the actual value to find the value of 1 unit.

Total Quantity

The total quantity of a **mixture** is always the sum of all its components: Total = Part 1 + Part 2 + ... + Part n.

questions.question: Rohan has notes of Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 in the ratio of 7 : 5 respectively. Monetary value of Rs. 5 notes is Rs. 575. What are the total notes of Rs. 2 and Rs. 5?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of **₹5 notes** = 575 ÷ 5 = **115**.

According to the ratio **7 : 5**, 5 units = 115 notes.

Multiplication factor = 115 ÷ 5 = **23**.

Total ratio parts = 7 + 5 = **12 units**.

Total notes = 12 × 23 = **276**.

**∴ The correct answer is 276.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of number of **₹2 notes** to **₹5 notes** = 7 : 5

Monetary value of **₹5 notes** = ₹575

**Formula Used:**

Number of notes = Total Value ÷ Value of one note

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0d83327dc07eef81e595632f46d6a97e871c2c0e971c76fdb486c041e299c8c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of **₹5 notes** = 575 ÷ 5 = 115

⇒ Let the number of ₹2 and ₹5 notes be **7x** and **5x** respectively.

⇒ 5x = 115

⇒ x = 115 ÷ 5 = 23

⇒ Number of **₹2 notes** = 7 × 23 = 161

⇒ Total notes = 161 + 115 = 276

**∴ The correct answer is 276.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Denomination and Value

The **monetary value** of a group of identical notes is the product of the **face value** of one note and the total **number of notes**.

Ratio Application

When quantities are given in a ratio **a : b**, they can be expressed as **ax** and **bx**, where **x** is the **highest common factor**.

Weighted Value of Currency

If number of notes are in ratio n₁ : n₂ with values v₁ and v₂, the **total value ratio** is (n₁ × v₁) : (n₂ × v₂).
